title: Absolute-Frobenius trivialization commutes with finite coefficient change
statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $X$ be a scheme of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]. Write $F_X:X\to X$ for absolute $p$-power Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. Let $u:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D_R=D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ of constant module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] for $R=A,B$, and ordinary derived scalar extension $T:D_A\to D_B$, $T(K)=K\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every integer $b\geq0$, let $\tau_R^{(b)}:L(F_X^b)_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D_R}$ be the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], iterated $b$ times, with its constant-coefficient identification; put $\tau_R^{(0)}=\operatorname{id}$. Let
$$
c_{F_X^b,K}:L(F_X^b)_B^*(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(L(F_X^b)_A^*K)
$$
be the inverse pullback coefficient comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), transported to ordinary constant coefficients through [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant]. Then for every $K\in D_A$ and every $b\geq0$ one has
$$
T(\tau_A^{(b)}{}_K)\circ c_{F_X^b,K}=\tau_B^{(b)}{}_{TK}
$$
as morphisms $L(F_X^b)_B^*(TK)\to TK$ in $D_B$. No flatness or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $B$ over $A$ or on $K$ is required. In particular $b=0$ gives the identity comparison.

proof.text: For $b=0$, both absolute-Frobenius pullbacks are the identity and the canonical coefficient comparison for the identity map is the identity. Since $\tau_R^{(0)}=\operatorname{id}$ by definition, both sides of the required equation are the identity of $TK$.

source.place: Final proof paragraph, convention $b=0$ and identity comparison

proof.text: Consider $b=1$. For every weakly etale object $v:V\to X$, the relative Frobenius $r_V=(F_V,v):V\to V\times_{X,F_X}X$ is the canonical isomorphism used to define the site trivialization in [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. The module version of that construction is exact and is induced termwise on complexes, as recorded in [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]. Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ using [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The comparison $c_{F_X,P}$ is represented by the coefficient-change pullback comparison of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), after the finite discrete coefficient identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant]. On each site object and each pure tensor $x\otimes b$ its two composites to $P(V)\otimes_A B$ are both restriction along $r_V$ followed by $x\otimes b\mapsto r_V^*(x)\otimes b$: the first applies $c_{F_X,P}$ and then the $A$-trivialization, while the second applies the $B$-trivialization to the same relative-Frobenius restriction. The equality extends from pure tensors to the tensor complex and is preserved by differentials; exactness and localization at quasi-isomorphisms then give $T(\tau_A^{(1)}{}_K)\circ c_{F_X,K}=\tau_B^{(1)}{}_{TK}$.

source.place: Final proof paragraph, relative-Frobenius section maps and passage to exact inverse image

proof.text: For arbitrary $b$, use the multiplicative-iterate clause of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] and the same clause in [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]: under the canonical composition identification, $\tau_R^{(b+1)}$ is the composite of $\tau_R^{(1)}$ with the pullback of $\tau_R^{(b)}$ (equivalently, the $(b+1)$-fold iterate of the one-step trivialization). The coefficient comparison in [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1) is compatible with composition of scheme maps, so $c_{F_X^{b+1},K}$ is the composite of the one-step comparison and the comparison for the $b$-fold pullback, with the coefficient-change comparison inserted at each stage. In the square expressing the $b$-case, whisker the already proved one-step square by the relevant pullback functors; paste the two commuting squares and use naturality of the one-step trivialization. The outer rectangle has top edge $c_{F_X^{b+1},K}$ and vertical edges the two iterated trivializations, hence is exactly the desired equation for $b+1$ after cancelling the canonical composition isomorphisms. Induction proves the displayed equality for every $b\geq0$. The argument only used K-flat resolutions to compute derived change of rings and never imposed flatness or Tor-amplitude on $B$ or $K$.
